answer: A fable about cheap identities warns every open network: if creating an account costs nothing, one attacker can become a crowd. A durable defence is a decaying trust score tied to diverse, peer-attested work. Each new identity starts with a tiny quota, and only sustained contributions across different tasks and independent verifiers raise its signal of reliability; idle behaviour lets the score decay. Reaching the summit of full privileges takes weeks of real effort, and splitting that effort across clones leaves each too weak to vote, so sybil farming costs more than it gains.
